title: Condition-before-estimate: finite Doob shell square-function for Q3 local likelihoods
question: Can conditioning a finite actual-Q3 history onto an increasing local coordinate collar expose an exact nonnegative Doob shell square function, separating local likelihood from remote influence without invoking a global Renyi or raw-energy norm?
method: Build the registered finite Q3 quartic onsite plus nearest-neighbour bond Hamiltonian and its Gibbs state on five volume/cutoff systems.
Apply both source supports and signs, both split term orders and signs, every partial prefix, both history adjoints, both beta values and both oriented coordinate collars.
Measure reference and transformed states in the product coordinate basis, form L=q/p, and compute M_r=E_p[L|F_r] from exact finite collar marginals.
Check the local identity Q2=1+chi2_local and the orthogonal finite decomposition chi2_global=chi2_local+sum_r E_p[(M_r-M_(r-1))^2].

Record unweighted and exp(2 mu r)-weighted shell profiles, rebuild the calculation independently, apply mutations that drop the local term or use an unconditioned parent, and compile Lean R398 for scalar positivity/bookkeeping.
finding: The condition-before-estimate decomposition is numerically exact on all 3,584 oriented history contexts. The primary lane passes 12,559/12,559 assertions, the independent lane reproduces the aggregates, the hostile lane passes 5/5, the integrated verifier passes 31/31, and Lean R398 compiles. The maximum identity residual is 1.0570971181733668e-18; maximum local Q2 is 1.0000033752914241; maximum global chi-square is 0.0002191742093816259; maximum unweighted shell cost is 0.00021579891795778293; and maximum mu=1/8 weighted shell cost is 0.00031475936144631414. The finite table therefore exposes a positive shell ledger and a local-vs-remote separation, but supplies no uniform bound.
decision_reason: This finite checkpoint advances the proof decomposition rather than the theorem tier. It turns the proposed folded-influence route into an exact, auditable shell square-function target and prevents a global Renyi or energy estimate from hiding remote influence. The observed finite shell profile is calibration only; phase conditioning, folded positivity and all regulator-uniform estimates remain open.

adversarial_review.check: The finite coordinate reference probabilities are checked before division and raw transformed diagonal minima are retained; positivity of an infinite-dimensional likelihood is not assumed.
Both right and left collar orders are recomputed, so the identity is not inferred from one preferred spatial orientation.
Reference and sample coordinate distributions are independently normalized and every collar marginal mass is checked by construction.
The hostile lane drops the local term and replaces conditional parents by an unconditioned baseline; both mutations exceed the preregistered threshold.
The finite Gibbs table has no phase label and therefore cannot establish within-phase contraction or mixture-weight preservation.
A finite positive chi-square decomposition does not construct the required positive two-replica Euclidean domination of a real-time contour.
Finite shell profiles are not promoted to cutoff-, volume-, source- or shape-uniform constants; common core, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS, gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A and Pre-A remain open.

next_action: Prove or refute a phase-conditioned folded two-replica domination and a source-, volume-, cutoff- and shape-uniform weighted shell square-function estimate on a Hamiltonian-derived common core. If the shell profile grows under a validated increasing-core stress, register that route-local obstruction before common-alpha promotion.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite coordinate-likelihood and Doob-shell diagnostic only. No phase-conditioned influence theorem, folded Euclidean domination, uniform shell bound, common core, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, mass gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure follows.
no_overclaim: The exact finite martingale identity localizes the accounting but does not bound the shell terms uniformly or prove a QFT limit.
